english.title: Adult meet a boy under 16 years of age following grooming
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person aged 18 or over, having on at least two occasions met or communicated with a boy under the age of 16, namely **(..SPECIFY VICTIM'S AGE..), not reasonably believing he was aged 16 or over,

(A)_[you intentionally met him]_
(B)_[you travelled with the intention of meeting him]_
(C)_[you arranged to meet him]_
(D)_[he travelled with the intention of meeting you]_

and you intended to do something to or in respect of him during or after the meeting which, if done, would have involved the commission by you of a relevant offence as defined in section 15(2)(b) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, namely **(..SPECIFY THE RELEVANT OFFENCE..)

english.notes:
(i) This offence is obsolete from 13th April 2015 following an amendment to the wording of section 15(1)(a). Where, previously, the offence required A to communicate / meet with B 'on at least two occasions', there is now only a requirement for 'one or more' meeting/communication. In relation to conduct taking place on or after 13th April 2015 Offence document H12211 should be used.
(ii) An act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which, constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 1st September 1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he/she may have proceedings brought against them in the United Kingdom (section 72 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003).
(iii) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act (paragraph 24 of Schedule 3).
(iv) The amendments made to section 15 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 by section 73 of, and Schedule 15 to, the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 are reflected in this version of this offence.
(v) There is no requirement that either communication be sexual in nature. The sexual intent must exist at the time of the arrangement of the meeting. An offence is then committed whether or not a meeting takes place. R v G (2010 EWCA Crim 1693).

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
